bench_setup = function() {
  options(ranger.num.threads = 1L)
  set.seed(20261117)
  t0 = 60L; k = 5L; n = t0 + k
  X = data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n), x3 = rnorm(n), x4 = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5))
  X$x1 = X$x1 + 0.6 * X$x2
  y = 1 + X$x1 - 0.5 * X$x3 + rnorm(n)
  miss1 = sample.int(t0, 6L); miss2 = sample.int(t0, 6L)
  X$x1[miss1] = NA; X$x2[miss2] = NA
  X$x1[(t0 + 1L):n] = NA   # each arrival is missing x1
  y[sample.int(t0, 3L)] = NA  # some earlier responses still pending, so y is itself imputed
  y[(t0 + 1L):n] = NA      # arrivals have no response yet
  dat = cbind(X, y = y)
  list(dat = dat, t0 = t0, k = k)
}

notes: Times k = 5 arrivals after t = 60 subjects (p = 4 plus y, ~10% missing in x1/x2): current refits missRanger (500 trees, maxiter 10) on all rows at each arrival; candidate fits once with keep_forests = TRUE and predicts each arrival (refit every k). This is an estimator change (imputed values come from different forests), so the expected verdict is 'faster, not equivalent'; tol 0.5 (absolute-ish on N(0,1)-scale values) only screens out gross disagreement. The predict path needs missRanger >= 2.6.0 (CRAN current is 2.6.1); arrivals miss both x1 and y, i.e. missRanger's 'hard case', which uses RNG (seeded) and iter = 4 by default.
